comparator.name: Bachelor Gezondheidswetenschappen, Beleid & Management Gezondheidszorg
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from the official 2026-2027 ESHPM Teaching and Examination Regulations and corroborated by the current programme and study-programme pages. The degree is 180 EC: four 15-EC thematic blocks in year 1, four 15-EC thematic blocks in year 2, and in year 3 a 25-EC free-choice space, the 15-EC Choices and Dilemmas block, and a 20-EC graduation placement and independent research project. The target and the official curriculum define no route requiring selection. The free-choice space is preserved generically rather than populated with an invented minor or elective topic.

components.name: Free-choice space
components.note: Open year-three space that may be completed through an approved minor, electives, exchange or international placement.

components.name: Graduation placement and research project
components.note: Placement-based independent research comprising responsibility for the problem statement, design, fieldwork and report.

alternatives.labelRationale: The curriculum concentrates on economics, finance, market structure, organisational governance, leadership, negotiation, law and policy. Health remains the evidenced application, while the visible label accurately signals that UCR supplies the underlying social-science and management fields rather than healthcare-specific professional modules.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest programme, this route removes most public-health, psychology and sociology study and adds accounting, finance, macroeconomics, behavioural economics, entrepreneurship, business law, international business governance, leadership communication, diversity management and negotiation. Eleven courses are shared and thirteen differ. Its organising choice is the financing, regulation, governance and management of healthcare organisations and markets rather than a balanced health-and-society curriculum.

alternatives.concept: A lifecourse and mental-health route connecting epidemiology and public health to developmental, social, abnormal, medical and clinical psychology; sociology and inequality; youth resilience; rights, ethics, public economics and political institutions; and quantitative, qualitative and evidence-synthesis methods.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum is dominated by psychology across the lifespan, mental health, public health, sociology, rights, ethics and public institutions. alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest programme, this route replaces economic-market, organisational and general biomedical courses with abnormal psychology, psychodiagnostics and psychotherapy, lifespan development, youth resilience, environmental justice and EU politics. Eighteen courses are shared and six differ. Compared with the markets route, only eight courses are shared. Its organising choice is how mental health, ageing, youth, social conditions and care needs develop across the lifespan, not the governance and financing of healthcare markets.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Epidemiology, introductory economics, law and sociology establish the health-systems and social foundations in semester 1. Research Methods & Statistics and Brain & Behavior precede all selected courses that formally require them. Biological health foundations, statistics and rights-based and comparative-political study precede the advanced health-psychology, organisational, economic, legal and social-theory work. The final semester consolidates econometrics, ethics, social psychology and public communication. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest programme integrates public health and epidemiology with policy, law, economics, organisations, sociology, health behaviour, ethics and mixed research methods. Two generator-eligible clusters support genuinely different routes: healthcare markets and organisational governance, and lifecourse, youth and mental healthcare. The technology-and-innovation direction is assessed separately but rejected because the available UCR technology and business courses cannot form a 24-course healthcare-technology curriculum without replacing healthcare substance with generic digital or commercial study. The included routes share 11 courses between the closest and markets routes, 18 between the closest and lifecourse routes, and 8 between the markets and lifecourse routes. Each pair clears the 4-course floor and reflects a different academic organising choice. The maximum of three alternatives is reached.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both examine health, illness, disease patterns and the evidence used to understand population health; the comparator integrates additional legal and patient-experience perspectives.
Both address mental health and welfare through social, cultural and professional perspectives; UCR focuses on psychopathology across the lifespan rather than youth-care policy.
Both examine changing needs across the lifecourse and older age; UCR provides developmental psychology rather than the comparator's integrated care-policy and ageing block.
Both examine how law, institutions and public authority organise social systems; the comparator applies economic, legal and administrative perspectives specifically to Dutch healthcare.
Both develop structured ethical reasoning about contested choices, rights and responsibilities; the comparator applies it directly to healthcare cases such as expensive medicines and big data.
Both analyse demand, supply, market structure, regulation and strategic behaviour; the comparator specialises these concepts in healthcare purchasing and insurance markets.
Both examine organisational change, innovation, technology governance and implementation; UCR addresses AI-driven organisational transformation rather than healthcare technologies specifically.
Both examine organisational structures, leadership, group dynamics, culture and performance; the comparator embeds these subjects in hospitals and other healthcare organisations.
Both culminate in independently conducted and reported research with practical relevance; the comparator additionally requires a healthcare-organisation placement and fieldwork over a 20-EC project.

The comparator integrates healthcare-quality measurement, improvement and regulation in a dedicated 15-EC block. UCR offers relevant evidence and policy methods but no scheduled course with the same healthcare-quality focus.
The comparator preserves 25 EC of approved free choice. UCR choice is distributed across each complete liberal-arts pathway, so no one scheduled course is asserted as its equivalent.

notes.text: The Erasmus programme is an integrated Health Sciences degree organised around nine healthcare-specific thematic blocks, health economics, health law, public administration, healthcare management, social medicine, methods, a 25-EC free-choice space and a 20-EC placement-based graduation project. UCR can combine public health, psychology, economics, organisations, law, politics, sociology, ethics and research methods into strong related pathways, but it does not reproduce the same continuous healthcare-policy curriculum, dedicated healthcare placements or profession-specific sequence.
